claims.text: An optimized CALPHAD-based framework can predict melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across a wide range of high-entropy alloys.
The framework can achieve agreement within ±5–8% of experimental values.
CoCrFeMnNi and AlCoCrFeNi are representative benchmark systems for the proposed broad HEA scope.
The target HEAs initially have stable solid-phase microstructures.
The CALPHAD database will be calibrated using fused high-throughput data from differential thermal analysis, modulated DSC, in situ density measurements, and synchrotron studies.
The thermodynamic database will explicitly include quaternary or higher-order interaction parameters.
High-throughput measurements will ensure statistically robust data across varied HEA compositions.
The model will represent solid and liquid phases using Gibbs-energy functions with binary, ternary, and higher-order mixing interactions.
Calibration of binary and ternary interaction parameters with fusion data enables CALPHAD extrapolation of phase equilibria and fusion properties.
Adding explicit higher-order interaction terms improves extrapolation across complex multicomponent systems.
Volume changes at melting can be estimated accurately using free-volume models adapted to the liquid-state framework.
The framework will predict melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, and liquid-phase properties within ±5–8% across a wide range of HEA compositions.
Kinetic effects can limit the framework's applicability.
Unanticipated higher-order interactions can limit applicability, especially far from the calibration composition space.
Higher-order parameter extrapolation may have reduced fidelity in highly multicomponent systems.
Independent measurements on HEAs excluded from calibration can test the framework's out-of-sample predictive accuracy.
A deviation greater than ±8% for any tested fusion property in any test HEA would invalidate the proposed approach.
